name: Work-at-home customer service representative (Foundever Canada)
summary: Foundever, a global customer-service outsourcer (formerly Sitel), hires work-from-home customer service representatives in Canada, with company equipment and benefits.
whatYouDo: You support customers of a client brand (e.g. an automotive company) from home, mostly by phone, after paid training with webcam on. You work rotating schedules that can include nights, evenings and weekends and are scored on quality metrics.
appeal: Employee role with medical/dental/life coverage, RRSP match, paid vacation and EAP listed
Extra $2.50/hr premium for bilingual English-French agents
Entry bar is moderate: high school diploma and 6 months customer service
watchOuts: Base pay on the posting seen was $15–$19.35/hr depending on province
Must be available for nights, evenings and weekends
Wired internet, quiet space and webcam on during training and work are required; background check
Foundever's dedicated 'Work at Home Jobs in Canada' page showed no openings when indexed; openings come and go
Reviews (anecdotal) mention low pay, demanding QA scores, last-minute program switches and short training

training.notes: Webcam required during training; a reviewer says new hires may go live on phones in week 2.

compensation.notes: Bilingual WAH posting (New Brunswick-based automotive account): $15–$19.35/hr by province plus $2.50/hr bilingual premium. Posting was ~5 months old when indexed.

reliability.notes: Full-time employee role; reviewers report schedule and program changes at short notice.

applicationSteps: Browse Canadian openings on jobs.foundever.com (Canada locations page)
Confirm the posting is work-from-home and your province is accepted
Set up wired internet, quiet workspace and webcam before paid training
fitsIf: You want a benefits-eligible employee job from home and can work rotating shifts, especially if you speak English and French.
notFitIf: You need daytime-only hours, can't get a wired connection, or want above-average pay.
